quickAnswer: A reliable weighted evaluation rubric for janitorial franchise vs local independent bids allocates 100 total points across five objective categories: Net Frontline Labor & ISSA Production Realism (30 points), Single-FEIN W-2 Payroll & COI Compliance (25 points), Supervisory Depth & Backup Rover SLA (20 points), Site-Dedicated HEPA Equipment & Chemical Specs (15 points), and Transparent Pricing & Termination Terms (10 points). Any bidder scoring below 75 total points or failing the statutory Workers' Compensation W-2 gate should be disqualified regardless of headline monthly price.

blocks.text: Why Standard Lowest-Price Bid Tabs Fail on Franchise vs. Independent RFPs

When corporate procurement teams evaluate commercial office cleaning proposals using a simple three-column price spreadsheet, the lowest monthly figure almost always wins on paper—and fails in the field within 90 days. Comparing a regional master-franchise broker against a direct local independent contractor requires more than checking who came in closest to $0.08 per square foot. Because the two operating models distribute revenue, insurance liability, and supervision differently, an effective weighted evaluation rubric for janitorial franchise vs local independent bids must isolate how much financial resource and management accountability actually reach your building each night.

In a standard 10,000 to 24,999 sq ft commercial office ($0.07 to $0.12 per sq ft benchmark) or a 2,500 to 9,999 sq ft suite ($0.09 to $0.15 per sq ft), labor and payroll burden represent 72% to 80% of total direct service cost. If Bidder A quotes $3,100 per month through a master-franchise clearinghouse that extracts 22% in royalty and financing fees, while Bidder B quotes $3,450 per month as a direct W-2 local independent operator, Bidder B is actually deploying $3,450 of operating value into your building compared to Bidder A's $2,418 net unit yield. Our 100-point scoring matrix exposes that gap mathematically so facility managers can defend value-based award decisions to CFOs and procurement committees.

blocks.title: Mandatory Pass/Fail Pre-Qualification Gate
blocks.text: Before assigning a single point on the 100-point rubric, enforce three pass/fail gates: (1) The exact legal entity employing the nightly crew must provide an active Workers' Compensation COI (NCCI Code 9014) with zero uninsured owner-operator exclusions; (2) The bidder must carry a $25,000+ Third-Party Employee Dishonesty Bond covering tenant property; and (3) The bidder must disclose the exact nightly labor hours committed to your facility.
The 100-Point Weighted Evaluation Rubric for Franchise vs. Local Bids

Use the weighted scoring matrix below during formal RFP evaluations. Each of the five categories is scored on a 0-to-5 scale and multiplied by its category weight factor to produce a maximum score of 100 points. To qualify for contract award, a bidder must achieve a minimum composite score of 75 points and score at least 60% of available points in Category 1 (Net Frontline Labor Realism) and Category 2 (Single-FEIN W-2 & Insurance Compliance).

blocks.text: How to Score Category 1: Auditing Net Field Revenue and ISSA Production Math

Category 1 carries 30% of the total rubric weight because no janitorial contractor—whether a national franchise brand or a 30-year local family company—can defy labor mathematics. Begin by establishing your building's baseline labor hours using the ISSA 3,500 sq ft per hour general office production rate, then adjust for your flooring mix and restroom density.

For example, take a 20,000 sq ft corporate office cleaned 5x/week (21.65 visits per month at the 0.90x daily frequency multiplier) featuring mixed carpet and VCT flooring (1.05x mixed flooring multiplier) and six restrooms ($15 to $30 per restroom per visit). Baseline general cleaning requires 5.71 hours per visit (20,000 divided by 3,500), multiplied by 1.05 for dual vacuuming and damp-mopping tool setups, equaling 6.0 labor hours per night—or 130.0 total labor hours per month. At the US standard billable range of $35 to $65 per hour, a sustainable monthly labor and overhead budget sits between $4,550 and $7,150 per month (before optional consumables at $0.012 to $0.025 per sq ft per visit or amortized quarterly deep floor care at $0.03 to $0.06 per sq ft per month).

When scoring a master-franchise proposal in Category 1, ask the bidder to state the exact percentage of the monthly invoice retained by the unit franchisee performing the work. Multiply their gross monthly quote by that retention factor (typically 0.75 to 0.85), then divide the net dollar figure by your 130.0 required monthly hours. If the resulting net field hourly rate falls below $35.00 per hour, award 0 or 1 point in Category 1—because the unit operator will inevitably shorten nightly shifts to survive financially.
How to Score Category 4: Auditing Commercial HEPA Backpack Vacuums and Hardware

Category 4 accounts for 15 points and separates professional commercial operators from undercapitalized crews. High-performing local operators and top-tier unit franchisees invest in ergonomic, sealed HEPA backpack vacuums that capture 99.97% of particulates down to 0.3 microns while allowing technicians to vacuum open office carpet tiles at 5,000+ sq ft per hour without snagging cubicles or tripping daytime staff.

To award the full 15 points (score of 5 x weight of 3) in Category 4, require bidders to list the exact make, model, capacity, and filtration grade of the vacuums they will dedicate to your janitor's closet. Benchmarks warranting full points include the ProTeam GoFree Flex Pro II Cordless Backpack Vacuum (6-quart capacity, HEPA media filtration, 18 lb weight with battery, and 75-minute cordless runtime ideal for eliminating cord trip hazards during early-evening or daytime shifts), the ultra-lightweight Makita XCV17Z 36V LXT Brushless Backpack Vacuum (2.0-liter capacity, true HEPA filter, 9.9 lb ergonomic frame powered by dual 18V LXT batteries for agile spot and workstation maintenance), or the versatile Milwaukee M18 FUEL 3-in-1 Backpack Vacuum (1-gallon capacity, HEPA filter, 15 lb brushless M18 design that converts seamlessly from carpet walk-ways to overhead HVAC supply vents and cubicle corners). Any bidder proposing residential bagless uprights or refusing to stage dedicated equipment inside your facility should receive no more than 3 out of 15 points.

items: Verify Battery & Filtration Maintenance Schedules: Ask how frequently HEPA filters and pre-filters are replaced on-site and confirm that spare charged battery packs are staged for cordless units.

Audit Supervision Ratios (Category 3): Award 5 points only when a dedicated non-working area manager oversees no more than 12 to 15 client buildings and conducts documented digital QA audits every two weeks.

Test Add-On Pricing Alignment (Category 5): Confirm that optional breakroom sanitation ($12 to $25/visit), interior glass partitions ($15 to $35/visit), and specialty floor extraction ($55 to $95/hr) match national benchmarks.

Require Direct Interview of the Assigned Lead: Make the final 20 points in Category 3 contingent upon meeting the actual field supervisor or unit franchisee owner who will hold your building alarm codes.

blocks.text: Worked Scoring Comparison: 18,000 Sq Ft Regional Headquarters RFP

To see how this weighted evaluation rubric works in practice, consider an 18,000 sq ft regional headquarters solicitation for 5x/week service (21.65 visits/month). Suppose Franchise Broker Alpha submits a quote of $3,400/month ($0.087/sq ft/visit effective rate), Franchise Broker Beta submits $3,950/month with a co-signed established multi-unit franchisee, and Direct Local Independent Gamma submits $4,150/month ($0.106/sq ft/visit).

When evaluated purely on price, Alpha looks like the winner. Under the 100-point rubric, however, Alpha's 24% royalty/note deduction leaves its newly minted single-owner unit with only $2,584/month ($22.46/hr across 115 required monthly hours), earning just 6 out of 30 points in Category 1 and failing the Single-FEIN W-2 gate due to an owner-operator workers' comp exclusion. Franchise Beta scores 78/100 because its established multi-unit franchisee furnishes a direct W-2 Workers' Comp policy and retains 84% of revenue. Direct Local Independent Gamma scores 94/100 by retaining 100% of revenue on-payroll ($36.08/hr net field allocation), staging two dedicated ProTeam GoFree Flex Pro II cordless HEPA backpack vacuums on-site, and granting a 30-day termination-for-convenience clause.

faqs.q: Can a janitorial franchise ever outscore a local independent operator on this 100-point rubric?
faqs.a: Yes. When a regional master franchisor assigns an established, scaled multi-unit franchisee that employs its own W-2 crew, carries full statutory Workers' Compensation under its own FEIN, pays a lower tiered royalty rate (10% to 14%), and co-signs the service level agreement, that franchise bid can easily score 80 to 90+ points.

faqs.q: Why does Category 1 weight net field yield higher than the lowest gross monthly invoice?
faqs.a: Because gross invoice price measures what leaves your accounting department, whereas net field yield ($35 to $65 per billable labor hour) measures how many hours of trained human labor actually clean your facility. A quote that yields less than $35/hr to the field entity mathematically guarantees corner-cutting and chronic staff turnover.

faqs.q: How should we adjust the ISSA 3,500 sq ft/hr benchmark for dense medical or high-glass offices?
faqs.a: For dense workstation layouts, ceramic tile and grout areas (1.12x multiplier), or suites requiring extensive interior partition glass detailing ($15 to $35 per visit) and breakroom appliance sanitation ($12 to $25 per visit), adjust the effective production rate down to 2,500 to 2,800 sq ft per hour before scoring Category 1.

faqs.q: What documentation proves a bidder's Category 4 equipment commitment?
faqs.a: Require the bidder to list serial-numbered or model-specific commercial equipment—such as ProTeam, Makita, or Milwaukee HEPA backpack vacuums—in Exhibit B of the proposal, along with a photo verification requirement within 48 hours of contract Mobilization Day.
